name: Eliphelet
overview: Eliphelet is a male figure known as the son of Ahasbai and is identified as the twenty-seventh member of "the thirty," a distinguished group of David's mighty men. While his tribal affiliation and additional notes are not recorded, his role among David's elite warriors highlights his significance in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliphelet means "G-d [El] is [my] deliverance," reflecting a trust in divine salvation. A variant name, Eliphal, meaning "[my] G-d [El] sit in judgment," is also associated with this individual, underscoring themes of God's deliverance and righteous judgment in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Eliphelet is the son of Ahasbai. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliphelet's mention as one of David's mighty men places him among the loyal warriors who supported King David during his reign. His inclusion in this elite group demonstrates his valor and importance in the establishment and defense of David's kingdom. The meanings of his names further emphasize a reliance on God's deliverance and justice, aligning with the faith-centered character of David's followers.
